title: The Miraculousness And Testimony Of The Quran 17th Degree 3rd Point The Challenge Of Eloquence And Its Inimitability

questions.question: What did the desert poet do when he heard one verse of the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He fell down in prostration.

questions.question: Did that poet say he became Muslim right then, or did he give another reason?
questions.answer: He gave another reason. He said he bowed because of the beauty and power of the words.

questions.question: What have many great language scholars agreed about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They agreed that people cannot match its speech.

questions.question: What challenge did the Qur'an give to proud speakers and writers?
questions.answer: It challenged them to make even one surah like it.

questions.question: What did the stubborn speakers choose instead of meeting that challenge?
questions.answer: They chose a harder path and put themselves and their wealth in danger.

questions.question: What does their choice show?
questions.answer: It shows they could not make something like the Qur'an.

questions.question: Have many Arabic books been written by both supporters and enemies of the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Yes. Many books were written by both sides.

questions.question: Were any of those books able to reach the Qur'an's level?
questions.answer: No. None of them reached its level.

questions.question: If an ordinary person compares the Qur'an with other books, what would he likely notice?
questions.answer: He would notice that the Qur'an is not like the others and is higher than them.

questions.question: Why can the Qur'an not be lower than other books, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because no one could truly say it is lower, so it must be above them.

questions.question: Who heard the recited verse in the story: a ruler, a poet, or a merchant?
questions.answer: A poet.

questions.question: What happened right after he heard the verse?
questions.answer: He prostrated at once.

questions.question: When people asked if he had accepted Islam, what did he answer?
questions.answer: He said no.

questions.question: What made him bow down?
questions.answer: The strong beauty of the verse.

questions.question: What did many expert scholars of speech decide together about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They decided its way of speaking is beyond human power.

questions.question: What small thing did the Qur'an ask its opponents to produce?
questions.answer: One surah like it.

questions.question: Did the opponents take the easy challenge or avoid it?
questions.answer: They avoided it.

questions.question: What does avoiding the challenge help prove?
questions.answer: It helps prove they were not able to do it.

questions.question: Who wrote the many Arabic books mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Some were written by friends of the Qur'an and some by its enemies.

questions.question: What main idea do the poet’s reaction, the scholars’ agreement, and the failed books all support?
questions.answer: They all support that the Qur'an is unmatched in its speech.

questions.question: Why is the story of the desert poet important in this passage?
questions.answer: It shows that even hearing one verse had a powerful effect on him.

questions.question: Did the poet bow because someone forced him, or because he was amazed by the verse?
questions.answer: He bowed because he was amazed by the verse.

questions.question: What kind of people are named as agreeing about the Qur'an’s special speech?
questions.answer: Scholars and experts in language.

questions.question: What does it mean that they all agreed?
questions.answer: It means they reached the same judgment together.

questions.question: What was supposed to happen if proud writers could answer the Qur'an’s challenge?
questions.answer: They were supposed to bring one surah like it.

questions.question: Instead of answering with words, what kind of path did they take?
questions.answer: They took a harmful and risky path.

questions.question: Why does the passage call making one surah the short path?
questions.answer: Because it would have been the simple way to answer the challenge if they could.

questions.question: What does the passage say about books trying to copy or fight the Qur'an?
questions.answer: None of them became equal to it.

questions.question: What could even a regular listener understand from comparing those books?
questions.answer: That the Qur'an stands apart and above them.

questions.question: What is one big lesson from this whole part?
questions.answer: The Qur'an cannot be matched by human speech.

questions.question: In the passage, what kind of person was the man who first reacted to the recited verse?
questions.answer: He was a desert Arab poet.

questions.question: How fast did he react to the verse?
questions.answer: Right away.

questions.question: What reason did he give for his prostration?
questions.answer: Respect for the verse’s powerful wording.

questions.question: What have many famous experts in rhetoric said about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They said people cannot reach its level.

questions.question: How did the Qur'an speak to proud experts in speech and writing?
questions.answer: It called them to try to make one surah like it.

questions.question: What can we infer from the fact that they did not produce one surah?
questions.answer: We can infer that they were unable to do it.

questions.question: Were only friendly books compared with the Qur'an in the passage?
questions.answer: No. Books from both friends and enemies were mentioned.

questions.question: What was the result of all those comparisons?
questions.answer: None matched the Qur'an.

questions.question: According to the passage, what would even a simple person hear in that comparison?
questions.answer: He would hear that the Qur'an is in a higher class.

questions.question: Which idea is stronger in this passage: that the Qur'an is ordinary, or that it is above other books?
questions.answer: That it is above other books.

questions.question: What question did people ask the poet after they saw him prostrate?
questions.answer: They asked if he had become Muslim.

questions.question: How did his answer still honor the Qur'an, even though he said no?
questions.answer: He still showed deep respect for its beautiful speech.

questions.question: What do thousands of scholars help prove in this passage?
questions.answer: They help prove that the Qur'an’s speech cannot be copied by people.

questions.question: What challenge was given to proud writers and speakers?
questions.answer: To bring one surah like the Qur'an.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention danger to their persons and wealth?
questions.answer: To show they chose struggle and loss instead of meeting the challenge directly.

questions.question: What is proved by choosing the harder path over the easier one?
questions.answer: That the easier one was not possible for them.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention so many Arabic books?
questions.answer: To show there were many chances to match the Qur'an, but none succeeded.

questions.question: Did books written to imitate the Qur'an do any better than books written against it?
questions.answer: No. Neither group reached its level.

questions.question: What conclusion would a common listener make after hearing the Qur'an and other books?
questions.answer: The Qur'an is not in the same rank as the others.

questions.question: What does this part teach about the Qur'an’s place among books?
questions.answer: It has the highest place among them.

questions.question: What happened when the poet heard the Qur'anic verse?
questions.answer: He made sajdah.

questions.question: What did he say was the reason for that sajdah?
questions.answer: He was moved by the verse’s amazing language.

questions.question: Besides one poet, what larger group also judged the Qur'an’s language?
questions.answer: Many scholars and experts of speech.

questions.question: What was their shared judgment?
questions.answer: Human beings cannot produce speech equal to it.

questions.question: What was the Qur'an’s challenge to people full of pride?
questions.answer: Make a single surah like it.

questions.question: What choice did those people make instead?
questions.answer: They left that challenge and chose a much harder road.

questions.question: How does that choice act like evidence?
questions.answer: It shows they could not meet the challenge.

questions.question: What two kinds of people wrote the many Arabic books named in the passage?
questions.answer: Friends of the Qur'an and enemies of it.

questions.question: What happened when those books were compared with the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They all fell short of it.

questions.question: What final idea should we understand from this whole passage?
questions.answer: The Qur'an’s speech is unique and above all other books.
